b2-33.title: A long flight
b2-33.story: Anna and Max booked a trip to Canada through a small [[tour operator]] in Kyiv. Their flight wasn't [[nonstop]], so they changed planes at a busy European [[hub]]. During the wait, Max wandered around the [[duty-free]] and bought chocolate for his sister Sofia. On the long second flight, a friendly [[steward]] let Anna peek into the [[cockpit]] before takeoff. When they landed, Anna remembered to switch off [[roaming]] so she wouldn't get a huge phone bill. A free [[shuttle]] took them to their hotel, but they both felt terrible [[jet lag]] that evening. The next morning, they flew to a tiny island on an old plane with a noisy [[propeller]], and Max slept the whole way.

b2-34.title: Buying a car
b2-34.story: Anna's dad finally decided it was time to replace his old [[automobile]], which was older than Anna. On Saturday, the whole family went to a big [[auto]] dealership outside Kyiv. Taras ran straight to a shiny red [[supercar]], but Dad just laughed and shook his head. The salesman suggested a practical [[sedan]] or a strong [[pickup]] for trips to the grandparents' village. Dad asked whether the pickup ran on [[diesel]] and how much fuel it used. Then he took the sedan for a [[test drive]] with Mama in the passenger seat. It had a small [[turbo]], so it felt surprisingly quick on the highway. When Dad pressed the brake [[pedal]] at a red light, the car stopped smoothly. Back at the lot, Mama noticed a tiny scratch on the [[bumper]], and the salesman lowered the price. Dad signed the papers, and Taras named the new car "Rocket."

b2-35.title: Biking around the city
b2-35.story: Last Sunday, Anna and Lisa went [[biking]] around Kyiv. Lisa rode her heavy [[mountain bike]], while Anna rented an electric [[scooter]] through an app. They started on a wide [[boulevard]] lined with chestnut trees. A delivery driver on a noisy [[moped]] passed them and waved. Near the river, they stopped at a war [[memorial]] and quietly read the names. Then they rode through a long [[tunnel]], where their voices echoed loudly. On the other side, workers were laying fresh [[asphalt]] for a new bike lane. A city [[inspector]] in an orange vest was checking their work. A speed [[radar]] by the road showed Anna's speed: 24 kilometers per hour. "Slow down, racer!" Lisa laughed, and they headed home for ice cream.

b2-36.title: Packing a suitcase
b2-36.story: Ira was packing for a two-week trip to Portugal, and she couldn't decide what to take. First, she put in her new blue [[bikini]], because the hotel was right by the beach. Her mom reminded her that evenings by the ocean could be chilly, so she added a warm [[fleece]]. Lisa, who was helping, insisted on a light [[poncho]] in case of sudden rain. Ira also folded her grandmother's soft wool [[shawl]] for dinners outside. Then she tried to squeeze in a long [[trench coat]], but the suitcase wouldn't close. "You're going to the beach, not starring in a detective movie," Lisa joked. Ira left the coat at home and put a red [[beret]] on her head instead. "Now I'm ready for Lisbon," she said, and finally zipped the suitcase.

b2-37.title: A trip around the world
b2-37.story: For a school project, Anna and Max planned an imaginary trip around the world. Their first stop was Norway, where they would cruise along a deep [[fjord]] and visit a museum with a real [[Viking]] ship. From there, they would go to England, where Max insisted on getting lost in a hedge [[labyrinth]]. Next, they would take a [[gondola]] through the canals of Venice. In Istanbul, they wanted to shop for spices at a crowded [[bazaar]]. In San Francisco, they planned to try dumplings in [[Chinatown]]. The trip ended in Australia, where Anna dreamed of feeding a [[kangaroo]]. Max added one last goal: learning to throw a [[boomerang]] that actually comes back. Their teacher loved the presentation and gave them the top grade.

b2-38.title: On a cruise liner
b2-38.story: Anna's grandparents finally went on the cruise they had been dreaming about for years. Every evening, Grandma sent the family photos from the enormous [[liner]]. On the first night, the ship's cinema showed an old movie about a ship that hits an [[iceberg]], which made Grandpa a little nervous. A few days later, they reached warm waters and went snorkeling over bright [[coral]]. On the way back, a black-and-white [[orca]] jumped out of the water right next to their small boat. At dinner, the chef served grilled [[mackerel]] with lemon and potatoes. Grandpa saved a piece for later, but a hungry [[pelican]] landed on the deck and grabbed it from his plate. Taras watched Grandma's video ten times and laughed every time.

b2-39.title: On safari in Africa
b2-39.story: Before Max's sister Sofia left for Kenya, her doctor gave her tablets to protect her against [[malaria]]. Her camp was just south of the [[equator]], so it was hot even in the early morning. On her first drive across the [[savanna]], she watched a [[gazelle]] escape from a hungry cheetah. That night, she heard a [[hyena]] laughing somewhere near the tents. The guide told everyone to shake out their boots, and the next morning a [[scorpion]] fell out of Sofia's left one. Later, they spotted a [[cobra]] lying on a warm rock and kept a safe distance. On the last day, the group drove north to a desert [[oasis]] with palm trees and a cool spring. Sofia texted Max: "Best trip ever, but I'll be checking my shoes forever."

b2-40.title: Through the Amazon and Andes
b2-40.story: Lisa's uncle, a nature photographer, spent a month in South America and told the family about it over dinner. He started his trip in the Andes, where a patient [[llama]] carried his heavy camera bags up the trails. High above the mountains, he photographed a giant [[condor]] gliding on the wind. Then he flew down to the Amazon, deep in the [[tropics]], where the air was hot and wet. His guide cleared a path through the thick jungle with a [[machete]]. On a boat trip, the guide caught a [[piranha]] and showed everyone its razor-sharp teeth. Every morning, they ate fresh [[papaya]] with lime for breakfast. Lisa listened to every story and decided she wanted to become a photographer too.
